newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Late Xmas surge benefits UK supermarkets.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Late Xmas surge benefits UK supermarkets.

text.p: British supermarkets should show steady sales growth as they report on the Christmas trading period from next week, analysts said, as a sluggish mid-December was countered by a strong run-up immediately before the holiday.
"It seems there could have been a huge late surge and generally, chains coped very well, they had plenty of fresh food supplies," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Market leader Tesco kicks off on Monday with its Christmas trading statement and is expected to show sales growth of around 7.5 percent, analysts said, on a par with levels reported at half year results in October.
Second tier chains Budgens and Somerfield report interim results on Monday and Tuesday respectively.
Somerfield is expected to see half year pretax profits of around 52.5 to 56.0 million stg in its first results since flotation in August, compared with 24.2 million stg previously.
It could pay out a first interim dividend of 3.2-3.5 pence, analysts said.
Somerfield was forced to cut its flotation price twice from an original 180-190 pence to 145 pence per share when it launched in August onto a market gorged by new issues.
Analysts warned, however, that its sales might not be representative of the sector, because of disruptions caused by a refurbishment programme during the year.
Expectations are for slight growth year-on-year in the Christmas period after flat sales from existing stores in the half year.
Analysts said that the top four supermarkets -- Tesco, J. Sainsbury, Safeway and ASDA -- were likely to have maintained momentum set earlier in the year over the Christmas period.

"We would hope to see an increase in purchases of luxury goods, which could benefit the top chains, while second tier stores might not see the full benefit of increased consumer spending," the analyst said.
William Morrison Supermarkets, a regional chain, said last week that sales excluding petrol in the five weeks to January 5 were up 1.2 percent on the year-ago period.

Morrison said petrol sales in the Christmas period were down 13 percent but analysts said it was not clear whether other chains would see similar pressure as a fierce price war last year between supermarkets and oil majors may have abated.

Sainsbury will report on Christmas trade on January 24 with Safeway on February 7. ASDA, which prides itself on being the cheapest of the big four, does not publish Christmas trading figures but a spokesman told Reuters the group had had "a very good Christmas and a very good New Year."
Analysts said Sainsbury, which has the highest sales per square foot of space, might have edged up same store Christmas sales from the three percent or so rise reported in October.
Latest figures from research group Taylor Nelson/AGB showed the chain edging market share up to 21 percent in the Christmas week from 19.6 percent a year ago.
Tesco edged up market share to 21.7 percent from 21.5 percent over Christmas, according to Taylor Nelson/AGB.
Safeway, seen as the most innovative of the big four, should also have hung on to the five percent rise achieved at interims in November, analysts said.

Analysts said margins for all the big four supermarkets might have shown some improvement, especially if customers had plumped for quality and value-added foods over the holiday period rather than focusing on price. "Consumer confidence and spending look to be both slightly up and supermarkets could have benefited from more of any marginal spending," one analyst said.
-- Jo Winterbottom, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
